items.problem: `efficiency` the `scan_users` query of a batch step grows with the number of users above `cursor_user_id` that have no lower version row. `WHERE u.user_id > $1 ... EXISTS (... s.contract_version < $3) ... LIMIT $2` stops early only after finding `migration.batchSize` matches, and `user_state` and `server_state` have only the key `(user_id, kind, item_id)` (server/core/storage/schema.ts:212), so each visited user costs two scans of that user's rows. The step that finds no user, which every batch must run to become `DONE`, visits every remaining `user` row. The query runs on `read_db` from job `migration_batch` (server/core/migration/index.ts:358), and storage.md `### DB adapter` says query functions are synchronous and that an answer later than `storage.dbAnswerWaitMs` closes the connection and is a DB connection failure. The duration was not measured

On PostgreSQL, a lock wait of 0 fails every transaction even when it would wait for nothing, because `open_tx` throws `NO_FREE_CONNECTION` when `wait_ms < 1` and `wait_ms` is the lock wait itself when no connection wait happened. `settings/core-settings.schema.json` allows 0 for `storage.userLockWaitMs` and `storage.schemaLockWaitMs`, and `open-game-works-core/skills/server-core/modules/storage.md:141` and `:263` fail only when the wait exceeds the value. Reproduced on the adapter against PostgreSQL 18.6 with an idle pool: `PostgresAdapter.begin({lock_wait_ms: 1, first: null})` is ok, and `begin({lock_wait_ms: 0, first: null})` is `DbError` kind `lock` code `POOL` "the wait for a free PostgreSQL connection left nothing of the lock wait". `is_db_failure` makes kind `lock` the `FAILED` of a transaction, so by code path `storage.userLockWaitMs` 0 makes the rate counter `run_game_transaction` `FAILED` and each request that counts it `INTERNAL` (`routing.md:174`); SQLite does not have this path. `storage.schemaLockWaitMs` 0 goes through the same line at server start: the `core update` report `records/1793768289963-update-core-mw1nbqne990438.md` observed that message on PostgreSQL only, and `server/core/routing/tests/settings-minimum.test.ts` keeps that key at its default. The same test sets `storage.userLockWaitMs` to 0 and passes because it checks server start only

In `run_user`, a function that returns a failure code makes it return that code even when the transaction is broken (`state.broken` set by `mark_broken` after a PostgreSQL lock abort in `lock_row`, `tx.ts:387`). It rolls back without returning `FAILED`. The same applies to `run_game` at `tx.ts:263`. `storage.md:151` says that after such an abort, "When the function ends, by return or by throw, ... the operation that opened that transaction is `FAILED`", and `routing.md:122` relies on that ("step 13 handles that `FAILED` instead"). Run path: the probe of R4-1 on PostgreSQL. `lock_game_row` of `coupon_coupon` is `FAILED`, coupon returns `INTERNAL`, `run_request_transaction` returns that code, and routing `finish` (`server/core/routing/pipeline.ts:701`) never takes the `FAILED` branch, so no `request transaction failed` `error` log was written. The same path also lets a content handler that catches a lock throw and returns a `GameError` respond with that `GameError` instead of `INTERNAL`

A transaction function can let out a `lock` or `connection` DbError that did not come from a statement of its own transaction, for example a `read_db` query inside the function that waits past `storage.userLockWaitMs`. `read_db` statements run with `owner` null (`server/core/storage/core.ts:196-205`), so `mark_broken` never runs and `state.broken` stays false. `body` still returns `FAILED` through `is_db_failure(error)`. `open-game-works-core/skills/server-core/modules/storage.md:348` (error table: a throw of the function on a transaction that PostgreSQL did not abort rolls back and throws) and `open-game-works-core/skills/server-core/modules/storage.md:155` (a `read_db` statement failure throws) say the operation should roll back and throw that value. This line existed before the range.
